fix_commit_message:
Strengthen the fts5_locale() function against integer overflow attacks, even when SQLite is compiled with oversize values for SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH.

FossilOrigin-Name: f0dbd9d22f558dd002e2132381de3c82d55a670399b3e527b5962b025141676a
agent_reasoning: Without this change, nLocale, nText and nBlob are plain 32-bit ints. nBlob = nLocale + 1 + nText is computed in 32-bit arithmetic and passed to sqlite3_malloc() (also 32-bit sized). On builds with an oversized SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH, an attacker supplying sufficiently large LOCALE/TEXT arguments could make nLocale+nText overflow a 32-bit int, wrapping to a small or negative value. sqlite3_malloc() would then allocate an undersized buffer, and the subsequent memcpy() calls (which use the original, non-overflowed i64-equivalent lengths) would write past the end of the allocation — a heap buffer overflow. Switching nLocale/nText/nBlob to i64 and using sqlite3_malloc64() ensures the size computation and allocation are performed with 64-bit precision, matching the real maximum sizes SQLite can represent, so the sum can no longer wrap and the allocation is always correctly sized for the subsequent copies.
